topics.name: Tenses: naming and changing (time and aspect)
Phrasal verbs and idioms (drop out, let down, drown out)

options: Jobs didn't have a dorm room.
Jobs didn't had a dorm room.
Jobs don't had a dorm room.
questions.rule: didn't = did not, and it is followed by the base verb: didn't have.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Steve Jobs starts Apple when he was twenty.
Steve Jobs started Apple when he is twenty.
Steve Jobs started Apple when he was twenty.
questions.rule: Both actions are finished in the past: started ... when he was twenty.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After don't, use the base verb: don't let me down (let someone down = disappoint).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two people (plural) and a past year (in 1976): didn't have.

questions.after: seven miles every Sunday for a good meal.
questions.rule: A past habit (as a student) in the simple past: Jobs walked.

questions.after: go to the party; I have an exam tomorrow.
questions.rule: can't = cannot, and it is followed by the base verb go.
A negative imperative: Don't + base verb.

chat: Are you coming to the computer club?
questions.rule: I'm = I am, so add the -ing form: I'm coming.
Imperative to passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: After to, always use the base verb: had to sleep, to get.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: I have never be so close to death.
I has never been so close to death.
I have never been so close to death.
questions.rule: Present perfect: have + past participle (been). With I, use have.

options: Let the work is done at once.
Let the work be done at once.
Let the work be did at once.
questions.rule: Passive imperative: Let + object + be + past participle (done).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two people joined by and make a plural subject: Woz and Jobs were building.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In look forward to, 'to' is a preposition, so use the -ing form: to hearing.
drop out of means to leave a school or course before finishing.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the past perfect.
questions.rule: Past perfect: had + past participle for an action done before a past time.

chat: I failed my first driving test.
options: Don't give up, Grandpa. Try again!
Don't gives up, Grandpa. Try again!
Don't giving up, Grandpa. Try again!
questions.rule: Negative imperative: Don't + base verb: Don't give up.

chat: What were you doing at six yesterday?
questions.rule: A past continuous question needs a past continuous answer: I was practising.

questions.prompt: Change into the present perfect tense.
questions.rule: Present perfect: have + past participle (lost). Had lost is the past perfect.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: can't (cannot) takes the base verb: come. After to, use the base verb: finish.
I'd better = I had better, followed by the base verb without to: leave.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous: has been + -ing: has been learning.
By + a future time takes the future perfect: will have finished.
The passive of an order begins with Let: Let + object + be + past participle.
let someone down = disappoint them; the object goes between let and down.

chat: Will you be home for dinner?
options: No, I don't. I'm staying at Asha's.
No, I won't. I'm stayed at Asha's.
No, I won't. I'm staying at Asha's.
questions.rule: Answer a will question with won't (will not). I'm + -ing: I'm staying.

chat: Why did Aman leave the team?
options: He drops out because of his exams.
He dropped out because of his exams.
He dropped out because his exams.
questions.rule: Past question, past answer: dropped out. Before a noun, use because of.
Imperative to passive: Let your heart be followed.

questions.prompt: Change into the past perfect tense.
questions.rule: Past perfect: had + past participle (designed).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Best in the whole country: the best. The story is in the past: it all came back.

options: Jobs said that he has dropped out of college.
Jobs said that he had drop out of college.
Jobs said that he had dropped out of college.
questions.rule: In reported speech after said, the past moves back to the past perfect: had dropped.

options: Let the lights are switched off.
Let the lights be switched off.
Let the lights be switch off.
questions.rule: Passive imperative: Let + object + be + past participle (switched off).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A negative statement (haven't found) takes a positive tag: have you?

questions.before: The noise of other people's opinions should not
questions.rule: After the modal should not, use the base verb: drown out.

questions.after: waste your time living someone else's life.
questions.rule: mustn't (must not) forbids something and takes the base verb: mustn't waste.
Passive of 'Announce the results tomorrow': Let the results be announced tomorrow.

chat: How long have you been learning the guitar?
options: I have been learning it for two years.
I have been learning it since two years.
I am learning it for two years.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous with a length of time: have been learning ... for two years.

options: You are requested share your wisdom.
You are requested to share your wisdom.
You were request to share your wisdom.
questions.rule: A polite order with please becomes You are requested to + verb.

questions.prompt: Change into the present perfect continuous tense.
options: Life have been hitting you hard.
Life has been hitting you hard.
Life has been hit you hard.
questions.rule: Present perfect continuous: has been + -ing. Life is singular: has.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: let + object + base verb: let others drown out. do not + base verb: do not settle.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tenses.
options: By the time Jobs returned to Apple, he has started two companies.
By the time Jobs had returned to Apple, he started two companies.
By the time Jobs returned to Apple, he had started two companies.
questions.rule: The earlier action (starting companies) takes the past perfect: had started.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Neither ... nor is already negative (no weren't), and the verb agrees with Jobs: was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: talk someone out of is followed by the -ing form: out of following.

questions.before: When the doctor called that evening, I
questions.rule: An action before another past action (the doctor called) takes the past perfect: had lived.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the future perfect continuous.
questions.rule: Future perfect continuous: will have been + -ing + for + period.

chat: Any advice for the new students?
options: Stay curious, and never stop to learning.
Stay curious, and never stop learning.
Stays curious, and never stop learning.
questions.rule: Imperatives use the base verb (Stay), and stop + -ing means stop doing it.

chat: Shall I book the tickets now?
options: No, you needn't to. I've already booked them.
No, you needn't. I've already booked them.
No, you needn't. I've already book them.
questions.rule: needn't = no need (no to after it). I've = I have + past participle: booked.

options: Let not your time is wasted.
Let your time be not waste.
Let not your time be wasted.
questions.rule: Negative imperative to passive: Let not + object + be + past participle: Let not your time be wasted.

questions.prompt: Change into the past perfect continuous tense.
options: My doctor had been advised me.
My doctor had been advising me.
My doctor has been advising me.
questions.rule: Past perfect continuous: had been + -ing (advising).

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this paragraph.
questions.rule: Passive: was diagnosed, could be cured (past participles). advised him to + base verb: go.
